label: Privacy and data protection
summary: Onboarding settles which privacy law reaches the organisation and in what role (GDPR role and EU reach, HIPAA status, Saudi PDPL role, NDMO basis) and a few facts that decide which duties apply; records, officers, contracts, transfers lists and breach handling are the compliance work that follows, and Saudi PDPL and NDMO items rest on secondary or unverified sources and say so.

source.ref: GDPR Arts 3 and 27 (reach, EU representative) with EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 (controller and processor roles) and 8/2022 (lead authority); fields for other laws carry their own source

fields.label: GDPR role
fields.note: Role follows who decides purposes and essential means, not what a contract calls it (EDPB 07/2020). Controllers and processors carry different GDPR duties, so the role decides which requirements apply.

fields.label: EU establishment
fields.note: Art. 3(1) reaches processing in the context of an establishment in the EU, wherever the data is processed. Without one, only the targeting grounds of Art. 3(2) can bring the organisation in.

fields.label: Targeting basis
options: Offers goods or services to people in the EU
Monitors behaviour of people in the EU
fields.note: Art. 3(2) reaches organisations outside the EU that offer goods or services to people there or monitor their behaviour there. If neither is true, GDPR does not reach the organisation; record that.

fields.label: One-stop shop
options: Applies: main establishment in the EEA
Not applicable: no EEA main establishment

source.ref: EDPB Guidelines 8/2022 on identifying the lead supervisory authority (supersedes WP244): a lead authority needs a main establishment in the EEA; an Art. 27 representative does not give one

fields.note: A lead supervisory authority needs a main establishment in the EEA (EDPB Guidelines 8/2022). It decides whether the organisation deals with one authority or with each national one.

fields.label: Lead authority

when.eq: Applies: main establishment in the EEA

source.ref: EDPB Guidelines 8/2022 on identifying the lead supervisory authority

fields.note: Supervisory authority of the main establishment: the single contact for cross-border processing under the one-stop shop.

fields.label: PDPL role

source.ref: Saudi PDPL (Royal Decree M/19, amended by M/148), its Implementing Regulation and the transfer regulation, as summarised by CMS in October 2025; the official SDAIA texts were not reachable

fields.note: The PDPL puts most duties on the controller: registration, data-subject requests and transfer safeguards. A processor acts on the controller's instructions (secondary source).

fields.label: SDAIA registration

source.ref: Rules Governing the National Register of Controllers and the National Data Governance Platform, as summarised by CMS in October 2025; the official text was not reachable

fields.note: Registration duties reach some controllers: public entities, controllers whose main activity involves sensitive data, and individuals processing beyond personal use. Conditions change; confirm with SDAIA (secondary source).

fields.label: HIPAA status
options: Not subject to HIPAA, aligning voluntarily

source.ref: 45 CFR 160.103: definitions of covered entity, business associate and subcontractor

fields.note: Covered entities and business associates carry different duties, and a subcontractor that handles ePHI for a business associate is treated as one. A provider is covered only if it sends standard transactions electronically.

fields.label: NDMO basis
options: Private entity: required by sector regulator

source.ref: NDMO Data Management and Personal Data Protection Standards v1.5 as described in consultancy summaries; CMS notes the National Data Governance Interim Regulations mainly address government data. Official text not read

fields.note: NDMO standards bind public entities; for private entities they apply through a sector regulator or voluntarily (unverified: official text not read). Record the basis relied on.

source.ref: GDPR Art. 30 (records of processing); HIPAA risk analysis (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)); PDPL and NDMO as noted per field

fields.label: Special categories
fields.note: Health, biometric, genetic, belief, union, sex-life or criminal-offence data. It changes which GDPR requirements apply (Arts 9, 30, 35, 37). Saudi sensitive data also affects registration and DPO duties (secondary).

fields.label: Cross-border transfers

source.ref: GDPR Chapter V with Art. 46 (transfers) and the Commission's adequacy decisions; Saudi transfer rules as summarised by CMS

fields.note: Whether personal data leaves the EEA (GDPR) or the Kingdom (Saudi rules), including remote access and cloud regions. It decides whether the transfer rules apply; the transfers themselves are listed later, in the compliance work.

fields.label: Processing record
fields.note: Whether a record of processing activities already exists (GDPR Art. 30; the PDPL expects one too, secondary). Only its existence is asked here; building or completing it is part of the compliance work.

fields.label: Record file
fields.note: Optional: attach the record of processing activities. It is kept in Evidence.

fields.label: Risk analysis
fields.note: Whether a Security Rule risk analysis of the risks to ePHI already exists. The Rule requires one; a missing or stale one only tells the platform where the compliance work starts.

fields.label: Analysis file
fields.note: Optional: attach the risk analysis. It is kept in Evidence.

fields.label: Domain scope

source.ref: NDMO standards v1.5 (15 domains; security owned by the NCA), as described in consultancy summaries; official text not read

fields.note: The standards set out 15 domains and leave security to the NCA. Whether all domains or only some apply is a scope decision (unverified: secondary summaries only).

fields.label: Data office

source.ref: NDMO standards v1.5, data governance operating model, as described in consultancy summaries; official text not read

fields.note: Whether a data governance office already exists. Setting one up is the first phase of NDMO work, so Not yet is a normal answer (unverified: official text not read).

gate.label: The GDPR role is recorded
gate.hint: Say whether the organisation is a controller, joint controller, processor or both.

gate.label: The PDPL role is recorded
gate.hint: Say whether the organisation is a controller, a processor or both.

gate.label: The HIPAA status is known
gate.hint: Decide covered entity, business associate or subcontractor; the duties differ.

gate.label: The basis for applying NDMO is decided
gate.hint: Record whether the standards are binding, required by a sector regulator or voluntary.

gate.label: SDAIA registration is assessed
gate.hint: Check whether the controller must register with SDAIA.

gate.label: Data leaves the Kingdom
gate.hint: The transfer rules apply when personal data leaves the Kingdom; if none does, this framework may not be needed.
